patches[] ORDER IS APPLY ORDER. Merge each as its own --no-ff merge, in this order.
Two branches lack the up- prefix because they are heads of open cross-fork PRs:
renaming such a branch CLOSES the PR (measured 2026-09-21 on #18307). They get the
prefix if and when those PRs close.
status 'fork-only' means there is no upstream PR and none is planned: the patch
is ours to carry and upstream_pr is null. Every other entry is 'open-upstream'.

A patch whose changes cannot exist on the upstream tag gets a stacked up- branch: its row carries depends_on and a base that is the dependency set rather than the tag, the branch is built on the merge of exactly those dependencies AT THEIR MANIFEST SHAS, it is listed after all of them, and it is fork-only. up-response-scope-think-budget is the first.

patches.note: 2026-10-14, v0.40.4: one conflict in the rebase, server/routes.go, in two commits (676357e0 and f8055cdd): upstream replaced the m.Config.Parser = "harmony" assignment with parserNameForModel(). Resolved so the branch's net change to those blocks stays nothing; both harmony blocks are byte-identical to v0.40.4's. No patch line reads m.Config.Parser. | 2026-10-14, 6c817c7c (think-budget 0f315b73): a think_budget value that cannot be read is a 400, not a 500 -- reported by xollama (#1316); every refusal wraps model.ErrInvalidThinkBudget and handleScheduleError maps it to 400; TestInvalidThinkBudgetIsABadRequest covers chat and generate. | SPLIT 2026-10-14 (f8055cdd, one commit on top of 44343159, owner's ruling): a thinking level is no longer a thinking budget. think is stock v0.40.3 again (bool or model-defined level, handed to the model as written, never a bound; a number in think is refused; types/model/thinking.go, openai/, server/prompt.go, model/renderers/thinking.go, cmd/ and their tests are byte-identical to the tag, and the two harmony max->high blocks in server/routes.go are restored). The bound is think_budget only (request options, else the model's PARAMETER), with its own type model.ThinkBudget in types/model/think_budget.go: a token count or a share name (minimal, low, medium, high, max; xhigh = max); a count written as a string is a count; a word that names no share is refused. thinkBudgetForCompletion, thinkBudgetForShow and llamaServerChatRequest read think only for off. Anthropic thinking.budget_tokens becomes think true plus options.think_budget. BudgetTokens, Level, IsThinkLevel, ThinkLevels and the int case of ThinkValue are gone: a consumer that called them takes ThinkBudget.Tokens. WIRE CHANGE for clients: a level sent to get a cap caps nothing now; send options.think_budget. | BEFORE THE SPLIT: REBASED 2026-09-27 onto v0.34.4, which is not a plain rebase: upstream #18473 moved ThinkValue to types/model and made thinking levels model-defined (any string is valid on the wire; a model with stated controls resolves an unstated name to its default, one without them is checked by ValidateLegacyThinking). The budget is ported onto that design: the integer budget, the level-to-share table, BudgetTokens, Level and the xhigh alias live on model.ThinkValue in types/model/thinking.go; ValidateLegacyThinking accepts minimal and xhigh; --think forwards an unknown name to the server instead of refusing it. Upstream tests that pinned the old rules were changed only where this patch changes them on purpose (minimal no longer clamps to low; an integer is a budget, 0 and fractions are still refused; xhigh is max). One new commit, 2a097aca: upstream resolves think BEFORE the budget was read, so on every model with stated controls (qwen3.x, gemma4, ...) a budget was replaced by the default level's share -- think:1500 reached the runner as 1024 on a 4096 window -- and an omitted think armed a budget from the default level. ResolveThinking now reads an integer as thinking on, and the budget is read from the value the caller sent, gated only on the resolved value thinking. Test-first: 6 of 12 cases failed before it. 2026-09-27, b463e532: golangci-lint fixes reported by xollama (#488) -- bodyclose in server/think_budget_resolution_test.go (read the recorder's Code, never open Result()) and a gofumpt blank line in server/routes_generate_test.go. `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=v0.34.4 ./...` over think-budget reports 0 issues.

launch: a session file stamped before the clock said start is not old
patches.note: Real defect, not a test artifact. codexAppRequestCursor.scan compares a filesystem mtime against a time.Now() taken moments earlier; tmpfs stamps mtime from the kernel's coarse clock, measured 4.55ms behind at CONFIG_HZ=250, so the rollout file is judged older than the session that just created it and skipped for the life of that session -- the count stays 0 however many prompts are sent. Two seconds of slack; the exact per-line filter is unchanged. Fixes TestCodexAppCountsOnlyOllamaRequestsInRegularProfile, which fails on any host whose temp dir is tmpfs. Not going upstream: ruled 2026-09-22, no PR to be filed. fork-only is the settled status, not a placeholder.

patches.title: fileutil: three permission tests assert the runner, not the code
patches.note: Test-only. TestWriteWithBackup_{PermissionDenied,FailsIfBackupFails,FileUnreadableButDirWritable} chmod a path then demand an error; root has CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and gets nil, so they fail for every build run as root, which is the container case. They already skip on Windows for the neighbouring reason; this folds both into one helper. Only those three -- the other twelve pass as root and still run. Measured after: root 12 pass 3 skip, unprivileged 15 pass 0 skip. Not going upstream: ruled 2026-09-22, no PR to be filed. fork-only is the settled status, not a placeholder.

patches.title: lfm2: keep a reasoning block out of the answer when thinking is off
patches.note: Carried from xollama@solidpc (mailbox #255). LFM2.5-8B-A1B reasons regardless of "think": false -- its official chat template has no off switch -- so setInitialState routed the whole <think> block verbatim into content. This discards it when thinking is off and the parser supports thinking, the way gemma4.go and laguna.go already do. Independent of every other patch: it touches only lfm2.go, in three hunks that miss up-think-budget's ThinkingTags addition, plus an additive test; base is v0.34.2 and there are no known_conflicts. Six new tests, three fail on the unpatched parser. Whether it goes upstream is the repository owner's call; fork-only until then, not a placeholder.

patches.title: llama: load a gemma-4 assistant drafter whose shape is left unchecked
patches.note: Carried from xollama@solidpc (mailbox #284; authored there as a836824b). A llama.cpp patch, so it retires on a LLAMA_CPP_VERSION bump: check_tensor_dims read gemma4-assistant's empty expected shape {} as 'must be a scalar', and its error path threw vector::_M_range_check from llama_format_tensor_shape(ne), so an E2B/E4B assistant drafter never loaded. The .patch blob (4f103fa6) is byte-identical to xollama's. The applier sorts by file name, so 005 applies after 001, models/003 and 004 regardless of merge order; replayed on a clean b10969 fetch (391fac16) with 001+003+004+005 and llama-server built. Independent of every other patch; its one collision is the README entry, see known_conflicts. Merge position here only follows the fork-only-before-stacked convention.

Merges cleanly onto think-budget with every other patch (cherry-pick 87a2f4c5); go test/vet ./model/parsers and go build ./... clean on both.

Before that it carried its own 945-line copy, which already had b4c58eee's quiet close and reopen bar; what it lacked was #18212's data model (reset_seqs, a list, where it had reset_tokens) and the --reasoning-budget-scope flag. dea66221's message says the old copy lacked the quiet close: that is wrong, corrected here. patches.title: modelfile: show writes only a carried TEMPLATE; create refuses a quote that swallows directives
patches.note: Two faults in the show->create round trip. (1) Model.String wrote TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }} for a model with no template layer (template.DefaultTemplate in memory); a create from it stored a Go template the model never had. Now written only when HasGoTemplate. (2) An unterminated quote on TEMPLATE/SYSTEM swallowed every RENDERER/PARSER/PARAMETER line to the next quote into the value; ParseFile now refuses such a value and names the line. Independent of every other patch; on v0.34.4 directly, listed last only because it is newest. On think-budget it cherry-picks clean (64f1ae1c); think_budget_message verified to round-trip create->show->parse on that tree. v0.35.1: a second commit adds CAPABILITY (a directive since upstream #18708) to the directives a quote left open can swallow; without it a template swallowing only a CAPABILITY line was accepted silently.

patches.title: renderers: render the empty think block back for a turn generated after it (qwen3.5/tev1, gemma4-large)
patches.note: Requested by xollama (#1306, owner 2026-10-14) for v0.40.3-xollama.5 with opencoti c13. With thinking off the qwen3.5 renderer prefills an empty think block and the history dropped it for a turn after the last user message, so the next prompt diverged right after 'assistant\n' and a GDN hybrid re-read the whole previous agent step. Such a turn is now rendered as generated; turns before the last user message keep the template form. gemma4-large: same rule for its empty thought channel, only where the message opened a model turn. Every registered renderer was probed for the prefix property: qwen3.8/ornith always render the block, qwen3-vl never emits one; cohere, cogito, deepseek3.1 and olmo3-think differ with thinking on as well (template design), so left alone. Measured through a private xOllama build (xollama dev 619f3ed5 + this diff, c12 .4 engine, CPU, qwen35:2b, xollama's tools.py): thinking off step 2 reused 757/778 (315/774 unpatched), step 3 1282/1303 (770/1254). Upstream PR is the owner's call. Independent of every other patch; merges clean on the apply-order replay (921c8d54) and cherry-picks clean on think-budget (b8715d15).

known_conflicts.resolution: both patches add a new top-level test function at the same point; keep both blocks. Reversing the order conflicts identically -- this is not an ordering mistake.
same shape: two additive test blocks at the same point. Keep both. Reversing conflicts identically.

same shape again, three files at once: up-think-budget adds ThinkingTagger and the ThinkingTags methods, up-toolcall-tags adds ToolCallTagger and the ToolCallTags methods, both at the same point.
